brief: Eric Peters frames the AI buildout as unprecedented and government-backed: a dialogue has Oracle's CDS blowing out to 450 still not breaking the Intel-Nvidia-Oracle-government financing loop, since Trump can lean on Ellison via Intel's government stake, keeping the trade circular ($43bln already made on the Intel position). Peters argues Anthropic's IPO-prospectus warnings about catastrophic AI risk and self-preserving model behavior will fuel the rally further, drawing a parallel to Greenspan's 1996 "irrational exuberance" warning, which preceded a 480% Nasdaq rally into the dotcom peak. A multi-manager PM (Alpha) says he underestimated this cycle: the deflationary AI narrative is wrong, only hard power constraints stop the buildout, and $2-2.5 trillion of capex should push nominal GDP toward 7%, making current 10-year yields look too low, so he sizes AI positions like long options. A systematic trading-firm executive separately says scaling simulations from a million to a billion improves margins, but AI prices abrupt, rare gap events poorly, which helps explain multi-strategy funds' recent struggles. US data turned soft (payrolls, confidence, claims) even as 10- and 30-year Treasury yields kept rising, Monday's selloff tied to Trump rejecting Iran's latest proposal.
